narrative: Material PL3__M91F4E56 exhibits lumpy demand with a strong statistically significant upward trend of +3.0 units/day over the observation window, combined with variable but short lead times (mean 0.62 days, CV 0.94). Demand variability dominates the lead-time-demand uncertainty (72% of variance), requiring a meaningful safety stock of 282 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The (r,Q) policy with EOQ-based order quantity of 1,188 units reduces annual costs by 84% versus the current SAP configuration by shifting from near-daily MOQ ordering to economically sized replenishments every ~8 working days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With 68% non-zero demand days, short but variable lead times, and a well-defined cost structure (known ordering and holding costs), the classical (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity and safety-stock-augmented reorder point is optimal. The material is not sparse enough to warrant intermittent-demand methods, and the upward trend is best handled by periodic recalibration rather than a trend-tracking model.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds: maximum stock position (SS=282 + Q=1,188 = 1,470 units) is well within the storage limit of 8,427 units. Service risk arises from the demand trend — if mean demand grows beyond ~500 units/day without policy update, the current safety stock will erode.
